verifications.claim: Signal is free.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Multiple sources directly state Signal is free.

verifications.claim: Signal is open-source.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'open source encryption protocol'; R2: 'open source Signal Protocol'; R3: 'Our open source Signal Protocol' and 'source code, visit https://github.com/signalapp'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm Signal and its protocol are open-source.

verifications.claim: Signal is a messaging app.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'secure communication app Signal'; R2: 'messaging experience'; R3: 'messaging app with privacy at its core'
verifications.reasoning: All sources describe Signal as a messaging app.

verifications.claim: Signal utilizes the Signal Protocol.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'end-to-end encryption (powered by the open source Signal Protocol)'; R3: 'Our open source Signal Protocol'
verifications.reasoning: Sources explicitly state Signal uses the Signal Protocol.

verifications.claim: The Signal Protocol protects all messages, voice/video calls, and file transfers.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'end-to-end encryption (powered by the open source Signal Protocol) keeps your conversations secure... every message, every call'; R3: 'strong end-to-end encryption... Send texts, voice messages, photos, videos, GIFs, and files'
verifications.reasoning: Protocol powers E2EE for messages, calls, and files as part of conversations.

verifications.claim: Signal is available for iOS, Android, Windows, Mac, and Linux.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R4: 'Android... iOS... Windows 10 and 11. macOS 12 (Monterey) and above. Linux 64-bit distributions'
verifications.reasoning: R4 lists exact platforms matching the claim.

verifications.claim: Signal secures all communication by default.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'Privacy isn’t an optional mode — it’s just the way that Signal works. Every message, every call, every time'; R3: 'strong end-to-end encryption that keeps your communication completely private'
verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm security is default for all communications.

verifications.claim: In Signal, messages are encrypted before they leave your device.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2/R3: 'end-to-end encryption' (standard E2EE definition: encrypted on sender's device)
verifications.reasoning: End-to-end encryption directly implies encryption before leaving device.

verifications.claim: In Signal, messages can only be decrypted by the recipient.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R1: 'impossible for tech companies and anyone other than the sender and recipient'; R2: 'We can't read your messages... and no one else can either'; R3: 'we can’t read your messages... Neither can anyone else'
verifications.reasoning: E2EE explicitly states only recipient can decrypt.

verifications.claim: Signal operates under a non-profit foundation.
verifications.label: CLEAR

verifications.reasoning: Sources confirm nonprofit operation.

verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: R2: 'No ads. No trackers... no creepy tracking'; R3: 'We know nothing about you or who you’re talking to... no data collection'

verifications.claim: Signal does not sell personal information.
verifications.label: VAGUE
verifications.evidence: R2: 'No ads. No trackers... not tied to any major tech companies'; R3: 'supported by your donations, not by advertisers or investors... no data collection'
verifications.reasoning: No data collection and no ads imply no selling, but not explicitly stated.
